description: Add an admin 'Delete device' action and surface cross-employee device sharing on the HRMS Attendance -> Devices tab. Two parts, both client-side and strictly additive: (A) a destructive 'Delete' button per device row that permanently removes the attendance_devices registration (distinct from 'Block'/revoke, which is kept as-is); (B) a 'Shared' badge on any device whose device_key is registered to more than one employee (the exact real-world case: key 07c04911 appears under both Pooja Malik and Kishan). The duplicate-detection logic goes in a pure, unit-tested helper in src/lib/hrms.ts. NOTE: a new idempotent, owner-applied RLS migration is required for the delete to actually succeed (see steps) because the Phase 2 migration only grants admin UPDATE on attendance_devices, not DELETE — the UI must degrade gracefully (show the error toast) until the owner applies it.
steps: In src/lib/hrms.ts add a pure helper next to the AttendanceDevice type, e.g. `export function sharedDeviceKeys(devices: Pick<AttendanceDevice, 'device_key' | 'employee_id'>[]): Set<string>` that returns the set of device_key values mapped to MORE THAN ONE distinct employee_id. Keep it dependency-free and total (handle empty input, duplicate rows for the same employee counting once). Optionally also export `deviceKeyEmployeeCount(devices): Map<string, Set<string>>` if useful to the UI. Add a short JSDoc explaining this flags device sharing / punching on someone else's registered device.

In src/lib/hrms.test.ts add vitest cases: empty list -> empty set; a key under two different employees -> included; a key under one employee (even with repeated rows) -> excluded; mixed list returns only the shared keys. Follow the existing describe/it style in that file.

In src/routes/_authenticated/hrms/attendance.tsx DevicesView() (~L1543): compute `const shared = useMemo(() => sharedDeviceKeys(devices), [devices])` from the already-fetched `devices` array (import sharedDeviceKeys from @/lib/hrms). For each row where `shared.has(d.device_key)`, render a small amber 'Shared' badge (reuse the existing rounded-full ring badge styling pattern used for status, with an amber/rose palette) near the device key, with a title/tooltip like `Also registered to: <other employee names>` built via names.emp.get() for the OTHER employee_ids on that key. This is the cheap client-side first win and must not change existing columns' behavior.

Add a 'Delete' action button to each row's Action cell in DevicesView, after the existing Block button, using shadcn AlertDialog from src/components/ui/alert-dialog.tsx (import AlertDialog, AlertDialogTrigger, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogCancel, AlertDialogAction). Trigger is a small destructive ghost Button with the lucide `Trash2` icon (add Trash2 to the existing lucide-react import block at the top of the file) labelled 'Delete'. The dialog explains that deleting permanently removes the registration and the device will have to re-register (and re-await approval if approval is required) on its next punch, and that this does NOT delete attendance history (attendance rows only store device_key as text, no FK).

Wire a `remove` useMutation alongside the existing `decide` mutation in DevicesView: `await hrmsDb().from('attendance_devices').delete().eq('id', id)`; if `error` throw new Error(error.message). onSuccess: toast.success('Device deleted') and invalidate queryKeys ['hrms-devices'] and ['hrms-pending-devices'] (same keys decide uses). onError: toast.error(getErrorMessage(e)). The AlertDialogAction confirm calls remove.mutate(d.id); disable it while remove.isPending. Keep Approve/Block exactly as they are.

Add a new idempotent migration file supabase/migrations/20260516000007_attendance_device_delete_policy.sql that adds an admin DELETE RLS policy on public.attendance_devices, modelled byte-for-byte on the style of 20260516000006 (header comment, `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS attendance_devices_admin_delete ON public.attendance_devices;` then `CREATE POLICY attendance_devices_admin_delete ON public.attendance_devices FOR DELETE TO authenticated USING (public.is_admin(auth.uid()));`). Confirm the next migration number is 007 by listing supabase/migrations (20260516000006 is the latest in that series; if a higher number exists, pick the next free one and say so). Add a comment that this is owner-applied and that without it the browser delete is silently blocked by RLS and the UI shows the error toast.

Run `npx prettier --write` on every file you created or edited. For edited existing files, verify no NEW eslint problems were introduced (compare `npx eslint <file>` counts against git stash if unsure).
acceptance_criteria: src/lib/hrms.ts exports a pure `sharedDeviceKeys` helper; `bun run test` passes including the new hrms.test.ts cases, and the new cases would fail if the helper logic were reverted (e.g. a key under two employees must be reported as shared).

The Devices tab shows a 'Shared' badge on every device row whose device_key is registered to more than one employee, with the other employee name(s) in the tooltip; rows with a key used by a single employee show no badge.

Each device row has a Delete action that opens an AlertDialog confirm; confirming calls a delete mutation on attendance_devices by id and invalidates ['hrms-devices'] + ['hrms-pending-devices']; a success toast appears on success and an error toast on failure. Block (revoke) and Approve are unchanged.
A new idempotent migration supabase/migrations/20260516000007_attendance_device_delete_policy.sql adds an admin DELETE policy on attendance_devices using IF EXISTS/DROP-before-CREATE idioms.
`./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`, `bun run test`, and `bun run build` all pass; src/routeTree.gen.ts is unchanged (committed only if build changes it).
findings: DONE. Files changed: src/lib/hrms.ts (added pure helpers), src/lib/hrms.test.ts (+4 tests), src/routes/_authenticated/hrms/attendance.tsx (DevicesView: Trash2 + AlertDialog imports, sharedDeviceKeys import, `shared` useMemo, `remove` useMutation, amber 'Shared' badge next to device key with 'Also registered to: <names>' tooltip, Delete AlertDialog after Block). New migration filename: supabase/migrations/20260518000002_attendance_device_delete_policy.sql (NOTE: orchestrator suggested 007 but 20260516000007 is already taken — next free sequential number was 20260518000002, since latest existing is 20260518000001). Migration adds idempotent admin DELETE RLS policy (DROP POLICY IF EXISTS attendance_devices_admin_delete; CREATE POLICY ... FOR DELETE TO authenticated USING (public.is_admin(auth.uid()))) modelled on attendance_devices_admin_update. Helpers: `export function sharedDeviceKeys(devices: Pick<AttendanceDevice,'device_key'|'employee_id'>[]): Set<string>` and `export function deviceKeyEmployeeCount(devices): Map<string, Set<string>>`. UI degrades gracefully: delete mutation shows error toast via getErrorMessage until owner applies the migration (RLS silently blocks DELETE otherwise). Approve/Block untouched. Verification: tsc --noEmit clean; `bun run test` 18 files / 289 tests pass (hrms.test.ts now 8 tests, was 4; total baseline 285 -> 289); `bun run build` ok; eslint on all 3 touched files reported 0 problems; src/routeTree.gen.ts unchanged. Prettier: SQL files have no prettier parser (consistent with existing migrations); all TS/TSX files prettier-clean.
